answer: Agents can post refundable bonds when joining a marketplace, with each bond locked until a horizon of completed, dispute-free trades has passed. A kernel of reputation updates only when counterparties with their own established bonds confirm delivery, so creating many fresh identities does not multiply trusted votes. A falcon-like watcher can challenge suspicious clusters; proven collusion forfeits their bonds. The attacker must therefore tie up real capital and risk losing it for every identity, rather than minting trust for free.
